fact: 1918年3月21日，德军从圣康坦附近的兴登堡防线发动「米夏埃尔行动」，即春季攻势的开始；德军在英军防线上推进最多约40英里（64公里）、占领约1,200平方英里（3,100平方公里），但在亚眠以东的维莱布勒托讷被挡住，攻势于4月5日结束。德军伤亡约239,800人，协约国伤亡约254,816人。

sources.title: Operation Michael, Wikiwand（英文维基百科条目镜像）
sources.quote: Date 21 March – 5 April 1918 ... Territorial changes Germans penetrate British lines up to 40 mi (64 km) while seizing 1,200 mi2 (3,100 km2) of territory ... Casualties and losses 239,800 254,816 ... The offensive ended at Villers-Bretonneux, to the east of the Allied communications centre at Amiens, where the Allies managed to halt the German advance

fact: 1918年8月8日凌晨4时20分，澳军、加军与英法部队在亚眠附近发起进攻，澳军正面推进11公里、加军近13公里；鲁登道夫事后称之为「德国陆军作战史上最黑暗的一天」。德军在这一天损失高达3万人，士气急剧崩溃。

sources.title: Australian War Memorial, 8 August 1918: The Black Day of the German Army（Meleah Hampton）
sources.quote: At 4.20 am on 8 August 1918 the Australian Corps — together with the Canadian Corps ... attacked the German lines near Amiens in northern France. ... the Australians advanced the line 11 kms on their front, and the Canadians nearly 13 kms. It so demoralised German general Ludendorff that he famously said that Amiens was “the black day of the German Army in the history of the war. This was the worst experience I had to go through.”

sources.title: Australian War Memorial, Turning the tide
sources.quote: with an entire sector of the German front destroyed and losses as high as 30,000, it was a truly crushing defeat and led to a sharp collapse of morale

fact: 1918年10月24日德国海军司令部下令舰队出海与英国海军决战，不愿送死的水兵哗变；舰只于10月29—30日夜间被命令返港，数百名「主谋」被捕并押往基尔受军事法庭审判。11月1日海军司令部拒绝释放被捕者，11月3日基尔爆发声援游行，军警开枪，示威转为武装起义；到11月4日，约4万名士兵、水兵与工人卷入，起义在古斯塔夫·诺斯克主导成立士兵委员会后被暂时平息。

sources.title: German History in Documents and Images (GHDI), Sailors' Uprising in Wilhelmshaven (November 6, 1918)
sources.quote: the German navy was ordered to set out for one last battle with British naval units on October 24, 1918. The war-weary sailors of the Thuringia and the Helgoland refused to obey this order. Around 1,000 sailors were arrested and sent to Kiel to stand trial before a military court. On November 1, 1918, the Naval Command rejected a request for the arrested sailors' release. Mass rallies and protests in support of the sailors followed on November 3. ... About 40,000 soldiers, sailors, and workers took part in the rebellion in Kiel and Wilhelmshaven. The Kiel uprising was quelled on November 4, 1918, after Soldiers' Councils were formed under the leadership of Gustav Noske

fact: 1918年11月3日基尔示威者与军警冲突中的死亡人数，来源不一致：一份研究作「7人死亡」，另一份作「至少9名示威者被击毙」。本包并列两说，不取单一数字。

sources.title: Constantine S., The German Revolution of 1918-19, History Today/Historical Association（PDF）
sources.quote: On 3 November a protest by sailors and workers in Kiel calling for an end to the war culminated in a procession to free the imprisoned mutineers. When this was fired upon with the loss of seven lives, the demonstrators fought back.

sources.title: German revolution of 1918–1919（英文维基百科条目镜像）
sources.quote: On 3 November, police and soldiers confronted a protest march by the sailors towards the prison in Kiel where the mutineers were being held. The soldiers opened fire and killed at least nine protestors.

fact: 1918年11月9日，首相马克斯·冯·巴登单方面宣布威廉二世退位并放弃皇储继承权，随后辞职并把首相职位交给艾伯特；下午2时左右，谢德曼在国会大厦西侧二层窗口向人群宣布「旧的和腐朽的，君主制，已经垮台。万岁新生的！万岁德意志共和国！」，下午4时李卜克内西在皇宫前另行宣布「自由的社会主义德意志共和国」。艾伯特当场质问谢德曼「你无权宣布共和国」。

sources.title: Deutscher Bundestag, A tour of the parliamentary district（PDF，国会大厦西阳台说明）
sources.quote: On 9 November 1918, Philipp Scheidemann, chairman of the SPD parliamentary group in the Reichstag, addressing the crowd gathered in front of the Reichstag Building from one of its west balconies, proclaimed a Republic. ... “The old and the rotten, the monarchy, has collapsed. Long live the new! Long live the German Republic!”

sources.title: Deutsche Welle, Long live the republic – November 9, 1918
sources.quote: At midday on November 9, 1918, he proclaimed Germany a republic from the balcony of the Reichstag in Berlin, even though he'd not been authorized to do so ... At 4 pm, an equally large crowd had gathered at the Imperial Palace in Berlin. There, Karl Liebknecht also proclaimed a republic. His speech culminated in the proclamation of a “free socialist Republic of Germany”

fact: 1918年11月11日晨5时，停战协定在贡比涅森林签署，敌对行动于当日11时生效。德军须在15天内撤出法国、比利时、卢森堡与阿尔萨斯-洛林，并在31天内撤出莱茵河左岸；交出5,000门火炮、25,000挺机枪、3,000门迫击炮、1,700架飞机、5,000台机车、15万节车厢与5,000辆卡车；协约国对德的海上封锁继续维持。

sources.title: Armistice of 11 November 1918（英文维基百科条目镜像）
sources.quote: Surrender of matériel: 5,000 artillery pieces, 25,000 machine guns, 3,000 minenwerfer, 1,700 aircraft (including all night bombers), 5,000 railway locomotives, 150,000 railway carriages and 5,000 road trucks. ... The naval blockade of Germany to continue. ... British Prime Minister David Lloyd George announced: "The armistice was signed at five o'clock this morning, and hostilities are to cease on all fronts at 11 a.m. to-day."

fact: 1918年10月初，德意志帝国任命了一个向国会负责的政府，任务是宪政与选举改革并首先争取停战；这结束了第二帝国半威权统治，被历史学者称为「来自上方的革命」，但几天后就被「来自下方的革命」吞没。

sources.title: Constantine S., The German Revolution of 1918-19（PDF）
sources.quote: It now appointed a government that would be responsible to parliament, tasked with constitutional and electoral reform, and – in the first instance – with securing the armistice. It heralded the end of the semi-authoritarian rule of the second Empire ... But within a matter of days this ‘revolution from above’ was to be engulfed by one from below.

fact: 1918年10月德国本土的每周配给量为：肉50克、脂肪57克、黄油25克、面包5磅、豆类125克、面粉250克、马铃薯4—5磅、果酱1磅、牛奶半升、糖1克。

sources.title: German History in Documents and Images (GHDI), Weekly Rations (October 1918)
sources.quote: Quantities were limited to: 50 g. (1.8 oz.) of meat, 57 g. (2 oz.) of fat, 25 g. (.9 oz.) of butter, 5 lb. (5.5 American lbs.) of bread, 125 g. (4.4 oz.) of legumes, 250 g. (.6 lb.) of flour, 4-5 lb. (4.4-5.5 American lbs.) of potatoes, 1 lb. (1.1 American lbs.) of marmalade, ½ liter (1 pint) of milk, and 1 g. (.04 oz.) of sugar.

fact: 1918年5月16日的法令把面包日配给量由200克减至160克，理由是等待乌克兰粮食运到；同一时期海德堡的一场科学家与医生会议向皇帝、首相与国会呈递决议，称婴儿、妇女与儿童的死亡率已升至68‰，并指出四年食物不足使平民「无法对疾病作出正常抵抗」。

sources.title: The New York Times, Warn the Kaiser of Hunger Peril, 1918-06-14（据美军缴获文件与俘虏口供）
sources.quote: this resolution set forth that the death rate among infants, women and children had risen to 68 per thousand ... It was also learned that the decree of May 16. reducing the bread ration from 200 grams to 160 grams, stated that the reduction was decreed until crops arrived from the Ukraine.

fact: 德国以借债而非征税支付战争费用：1914至1918年，政府与私人用途的纸币总量由23.7亿马克增至331.1亿马克，批发物价指数（1913=100）上涨逾245%；马克对美元汇率由1914年的4.21跌至1918年底的8.28。另有资料作1918年底8.91马克兑1美元。

sources.title: Ebeling R. M., The Lasting Legacies of World War I: Big Government, Paper Money and Inflation（Nassau Institute PDF）
sources.quote: During the four years of war, from 1914 to 1918, the total quantity of paper money created for German government and private sector spending went from 2.37 billion to 33.11 billion marks. By an index of wholesale prices (with 1913 equal to 100), prices had increased more than 245 percent ... In 1914, 4.21 marks traded for one dollar on the foreign exchange market. By the end of 1918, the mark had fallen to 8.28 to the dollar.

sources.title: Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic（英文维基百科条目存档，JCU ResearchOnline）
sources.quote: The result was that the exchange rate of the Mark against the US dollar fell steadily throughout the war to 8.91 Marks per dollar.

fact: 按 Johnson 与 Mueller 的跨国统计，德国在1918—1919年流感大流行中的死亡数为225,330人、死亡率3.8‰；同一张表列法国24万（7.3‰）、英国与威尔士约20万（5.8‰）、美国67.5万（6.5‰）。各国统计口径差异很大，本包不把该表当作唯一结论。

sources.title: Ager P., et al., The Redistributive Effects of Pandemics: Evidence of the Spanish Flu, LSE Economic History Working Paper 308（表1，据 Johnson & Mueller 2002）
sources.quote: Germany 225,330 3.8 ... France 240,000 7.3 ... England and Wales approx. 200,000 5.8 ... US 675,000 6.5 ... Table 1: Mortality rates per 1,000, Spanish Flu. Sources: Johnson and Mueller (2002)

fact: 哈伯-博施法由弗里茨·哈伯开发、卡尔·博施实现工业化，是第一个在高压下进行化学反应的工业流程；哈伯因该方法获1918年诺贝尔化学奖。到1918年，该法已使此前的氰氨法「过时」，并在后世成为世界化学工业的基础流程之一。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Haber-Bosch process
sources.quote: developed by the German physical chemist Fritz Haber. He received the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 1918 for this method, which made the manufacture of ammonia economically feasible. ... Haber-Bosch was the first industrial chemical process to use high pressure for a chemical reaction. ... the cyanamide process was utilized on a large scale by several countries before and during World War I, but it too was energy-intensive, and by 1918 the Haber-Bosch process had rendered it obsolete.
